Distribution-based (provisional) MCID

Source: R/thresholds-mcid.R
mcid_distribution.Rd

Compute a distribution-based MCID and return it as symmetric mcid_thresholds() marked provisional = TRUE. This is never done automatically: you must call it explicitly.

Usage

mcid_distribution(
  sd,
  method = c("half_sd", "sem", "one_fifth_sd"),
  reliability = NULL,
  direction = c("higher_better", "lower_better")
)

Arguments

sd

Standard deviation of the outcome (in the population the MCID should describe, usually baseline SD).

method

"half_sd", "sem" or "one_fifth_sd".

reliability

Reliability coefficient of the instrument (e.g. test-retest ICC), required for method = "sem".

direction

Passed to mcid_thresholds().

Value

An mcid_thresholds() object with provisional = TRUE.

Details

  • "half_sd": 0.5 * sd (Norman, Sloan & Wyrwich 2003).

  • "one_fifth_sd": 0.2 * sd, a convention equal to Cohen's "small" d.

  • "sem": one standard error of measurement, sd * sqrt(1 - reliability) (Wyrwich, Tierney & Wolinsky 1999); requires reliability.

Why "provisional"

Distribution-based values describe the spread or the measurement error of a score, not what patients regard as a worthwhile change. McGlothlin & Lewis (2014) object that such values are not patient-derived and should not be treated as an MCID in their own right; anchor-based estimates are preferred. The legend of geom_mcid_zones() is therefore titled "MCID (provisional, distribution-based)".

Note also that half an SD is exactly Cohen's "medium" standardised difference (d = 0.5) and one fifth of an SD is his "small" (d = 0.2). A distribution-based MCID therefore adds no clinical information beyond geom_es_zones() with es_benchmarks("cohen_d"); it only relabels effect-size zones in clinical language.

References

Norman GR, Sloan JA, Wyrwich KW (2003). Interpretation of changes in health-related quality of life: the remarkable universality of half a standard deviation. Medical Care 41(5):582-592. doi:10.1097/01.mlr.0000062554.74615.4c

Wyrwich KW, Tierney WM, Wolinsky FD (1999). Further evidence supporting an SEM-based criterion for identifying meaningful intra-individual changes in health-related quality of life. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 52(9):861-873. doi:10.1016/s0895-4356(99)00071-2

McGlothlin AE, Lewis RJ (2014). Minimal clinically important difference: defining what really matters to patients. JAMA 312(13):1342-1343. doi:10.1001/jama.2014.13128

Examples

mcid_distribution(sd = 10)
#> <mcid_thresholds> (higher_better)
#> harm: difference < -5
#> trivial: between -5 and 5
#> benefit: difference > 5
#> Provisional: not derived from patients' judgements.
#> Source: Half SD = 0.5 x 10 = 5. Norman GR, Sloan JA, Wyrwich KW (2003). Med
#> Care 41(5):582-592. doi:10.1097/01.mlr.0000062554.74615.4c. Equal to Cohen's
#> 'medium' d = 0.5. Distribution-based values are not patient-derived (McGlothlin
#> AE, Lewis RJ (2014). JAMA 312(13):1342-1343, doi:10.1001/jama.2014.13128) and
#> are provisional until an anchor-based MCID is available.
mcid_distribution(sd = 10, method = "sem", reliability = 0.84)
#> <mcid_thresholds> (higher_better)
#> harm: difference < -4
#> trivial: between -4 and 4
#> benefit: difference > 4
#> Provisional: not derived from patients' judgements.
#> Source: One SEM = SD x sqrt(1 - reliability) = 10 x sqrt(1 - 0.84) = 4.
#> SEM-based criterion: Wyrwich KW, Tierney WM, Wolinsky FD (1999). J Clin
#> Epidemiol 52(9):861-873. doi:10.1016/s0895-4356(99)00071-2. Distribution-based
#> values are not patient-derived (McGlothlin AE, Lewis RJ (2014). JAMA
#> 312(13):1342-1343, doi:10.1001/jama.2014.13128) and are provisional until an
#> anchor-based MCID is available.
